To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the level of channel power is positively related to the use of equity incentives and negatively related to the use the instrumental incentives, while the use of instrumental incentives is negatively related to the level of channel conflict; and (2) the use of both types of channel incentives is positively related to channel performance.

the type of incentive used is determined by the level of trust, the level of dependence, and the level of power in a channel relationship, and that instrumental incentives are positively related to distributor compliance and equity incentives are positively related with both distributor compliance and distributor retention.
the use of equity incentives is associated with higher levels of relational performance, and the use of instrumental incentives is associated with lower levels of relational performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the governance of marketing channel relationships, and in particular with the role that incentives play in this process.
how marketing channels are governed and the consequences of these mechanisms for channel performance.
the governance of the marketing channel and how the channel members manage the relationships between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of channel incentives is an important and timely area of research, and the authors' work makes significant contributions to this literature.
channel incentive mechanisms are an important governance process in maintaining and extending the life of a marketing channel relationship.
this study provides an in depth look into how channel incentives can be used as a governance mechanism to maintain and extend channel relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more interdependent and trusting a relationship is, the more likely it is that equity incentives will be used to manage the relationship.

the use of equity incentives is more likely to occur when channel members have a high degree of trust and commitment in the channel relationship, and when the channel members perceive that the relationship is characterized by a high degree of interdependence and a high level of conflict.

the type of incentive used in a channel relationship depends upon the type of relationship between the channel partners, and the type of incentive has a differential effect on channel partner performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of equity incentives is more likely when a manufacturer is more dependent on a distributor, when the distributor is more powerful in the channel relationship, when the manufacturer has more power, and when the manufacturer is less concerned with distributor opportunism.
marketing channel managers need to consider the nature and quality of the channel relationship when determining the type of incentive to employ.
channel incentives are not simply an extra-contractual means of maintaining a relationship.
